item.title: Emacs Windows Installation
item.description:
Problems with installing

  1. Not having msys2 so that pdftools can’t build [install msys]

  2. Not having mingw so that sqlite can’t build for org-roam [choco install mingw] Don’t even have to do that. The mingw is installed by msys2. So go to mysys2: there will be folder named mingw64. Add it’s bin to the PATH.

       pacman -Syu
   pacman -S base-devel
   pacman -S mingw-w64-x86_64-toolchain
   pacman -S mingw-w64-x86_64-zlib
   pacman -S mingw-w64-x86_64-libpng
   pacman -S mingw-w64-x86_64-poppler
   pacman -S mingw-w64-x86_64-imagemagick

  3. Then find a version that supports modules : emax64. This is a well off version and has binaries in different places and things like that because it tries providing it’s own configuration.

  4. Helm-rg didn’t work for me. So, I installed helm-ag and used rg’s executable with it. All is in config file.

  5. Helm-rg will try to say projectile to add itself as well so, don’t use +fuzzy tag with helm.

item.title: Subconscious Reprogramming
item.description:
Link:How To Reprogram Subconscious Mind: The one cycle that determines your fate (Dirty Secret) - YouTube - Brave

Overall flow:

Thoughts[Incoming/Outgoing] –> Emotion Emotions –> Belief Belief –> RAS ( Reticular Activating System ) RAS –> Confirmation Confirmation –> Conviction

  1. Thoughts and emotions switch between each other for some time to form belief. You don’t choose incoming thoughts: these happen and most of us subconsciously create emotion out of it; then switch back and forth between more thoughts and more emotions.
  2. Confirmation is when you search for more proof to confirm your belief that you made.
  3. Strong proofs lead to conviction.

We have a habit of getting stuck in convictions. Even if we want to change conviction we cannot for most of the time. So, we need to break the whole cycle to break or change a conviction that we have.

    Speaking —talking out loud fluently and without hesitation Arguing —condensing what you say into a persuasive point(s) Listening —hearing and understanding the points others make Synthesizing —matching the points you and others make Arranging —structuring your points into a persuasive speec

  • Page 19 Highlight: “Switch”

  • Page 19 Highlight:

    Excellent listening skills are needed to follow the thread of an argument and be able to continue it without pause;

  • Page 20 Highlight:

    Each person picks a question, reads it, and gives a clear, fluent, and persuasive one-minute answer.

  • Page 20 Highlight:

    great activity based on a peculiar premise —you are a famous person of your choice in a hot air balloon hurtling toward the earth.

  • Page 23 Highlight: “Points of Information,”

    Although people speak as individuals, they are judged as teams of two, making the same case and supporting each other’s arguments.

  • Page 24 Highlight: “structure their speeches and label their points.”

    have to learn to handle situations, respond to the brilliance or failures of others, and keep listening to the debate while developing your own thoughts. Y

  • Page 31 Highlight:

  • Page 31 Highlight:

    casefile that contains notes from previous debates, ideas they had on all those topics, related articles, and background information

  • Page 32 Highlight:

  • Page 32 Highlight: “being over-prepared is worse than being underprepared.”

  • Page 32 Highlight:

    debate well, you need to take risks —postponing your commitment to your position to the last possible moment and ensuring that what you say is of maximum relevance to the live debate.

  • Page 32 Highlight:

    The final thought on preparation time is that you should prioritize the first speaker in the team.

  • Page 32 Highlight: “equity or the relative knowledge base”

  • Page 33 Highlight:

    motion is about space exploration, why not give her all the complicated arguments about the practicalities of travel through the cosmos while you talk about cost and politics?

  • Page 33 Highlight: “moral versus practical or political/economic/ social.”

  • Page 33 Highlight:

    Any number of clever, innovative, and brilliant arguments are not going to win you a debate unless they are deployed as part of a winning case

  • Page 33 Highlight: “—being flexible, broad-minded, and ready for everything”

  • Page 33 Highlight: “Defining the motion”

  • Page 34 Highlight:

    The definition should state the issue (or issues) for debate arising out of the motion and state the meaning of any terms in the motion which require interpretation.

  • Page 34 Highlight:

    A parent who smacks their child’s arm to keep her from immediate danger is acting out of necessity. A parent who smacks their child as a physical punishment, for something they did in the past, is acting out of cruelty. Children should be protected, through a new law, from this abuse by adults of their power.
